business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (extended to Bermuda and Gibraltar by the United Kingdom)

Gibraltar: Companies Act 2014 (as amended); Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; Financial Services (Investment and Fiduciary Services) Act 2018; AML/CFT Code of Practice 2020 (GFSC); Beneficial Ownership (Access) Regulations 2018; Sanctions Act 2019 and Sanctions Regulations 2020; Money Laundering Regulations 2019.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all UBOs (25% threshold), directors, officers, and local compliance officers against: UN Security Council Consolidated List; UK OFSI Consolidated List; OFAC SDN/Non-SDN Lists; EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database; Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2020 and GFSC public statements; FATF high-risk jurisdiction list; Interpol notices; global PEP databases. Given ISIC 4791 (online jewelry and fine timepieces) and Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier: mandatory enhanced due diligence under Gibraltar AML/CFT Code 2020 Part IV and Bermuda Proceeds of Crime Regulations 2018 reg. 11; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification mandatory for each UBO where projected annual settlement volume via Stripe or PayPal exceeds USD 250,000; annual re-screening and event-driven re-KYC additionally required; enhanced payout monitoring for cash-equivalent high-value goods.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies - corporate name search portal (www.roc.gov.bm); Gibraltar Companies Registry - GFSC company search and e-registry portal (www.gfsc.gi)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory English/Roman-script corporate names in both Bermuda and Gibraltar; no transliteration into secondary scripts accepted; registered name must end with the word Limited in the case of a Bermuda Exempted Company; stylistic, symbolic, or non-Latin characters are not permitted in the certified registry name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (mandatory suffix; consistency required on all documents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection: (i) the applicant may obtain a one-time 30-day extension of an unreserved name in Bermuda by written request to the Registrar of Companies before expiry; (ii) resubmit an amended name to the Bermuda Registrar within 14 days; (iii) file a written administrative appeal with the Gibraltar Companies Registry within 21 days of a Gibraltar refusal; (iv) if refused at administrative level, institute judicial review in the Supreme Court of Bermuda or the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under the Companies Act 2014 ss. 30-36; the final appellate tier is the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A Bermuda Exempted Company must maintain a physical registered office in Bermuda; a virtual office is acceptable only where the address belongs to a licensed corporate services provider with mail-handling and statutory records facilities. For Gibraltar external registration, a physical Gibraltar address for service of process is mandatory; a remote-only virtual address without a Gibraltar compliance desk is not sufficient for GFSC oversight or for Stripe/PayPal underwriting. Flex-desk or co-working registered offices are accepted by the registry, but materially increase payment-processor onboarding friction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-High: approximately 30-40% probability of an unannounced administrative inspection by GFSC/Gibraltar FIU within the first 18 months for an online-retail registered branch; approximately 15% probability of a Bermuda Registrar of Companies periodic compliance audit; probability rises to approximately 65% upon any PEP or sanctions screening trigger, or where a single timepiece transaction exceeds EUR 10,000 (triggering enhanced customer due diligence).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act (Cap. 147), Part IX (Continuation of Companies), sections 129-140, read with the Companies (Continuation) Regulations; Bermuda Companies Act 1981, sections 14-17 (Exempted Companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies House Gibraltar, Waterport Place, Gibraltar, via the official e-Registry portal at companieshouse.gi; cooperating with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies for the initial consent to continue.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO/1 (Application for Continuation) and the Gibraltar Certificate of Continuance, together with the adopted Gibraltar Memorandum and Articles of Association and the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required. The Company may adopt a nominal share capital of US$1 or such subscription amount stated in the share allotment schedule; no escrow account, capital deposit, or bank lock-in is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the Company, being a Bermuda Exempted Company, approves and adopts the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association for continuance as a Gibraltar exempted company under Companies Act (Cap. 147). (2) The members' share subscriptions and allotments set forth in the attached register are ratified. (3) The registered office in Gibraltar is established at the address in Schedule B. (4) The persons in Schedule A are appointed as first directors, CEO, CFO, and Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual meeting. (5) Any one director is authorised to execute continuation filings and pay state fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Bermuda Consent and Exempted Status Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Hamilton, Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an Application for Consent to Continuance (Form SC2) with the Bermuda Registrar, attaching the existing certificate of incorporation, a board solvency declaration, and a certificate of good standing. The Registrar will issue a Certificate of No Objection authorising the company to continue in Gibraltar. Ensure the Bermuda exempted status remains valid until the Gibraltar Certificate of Continuance is issued.
required_dossiers: Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association (Bermuda)
Certificate of Good Standing from Bermuda Registrar
Board Solvency Declaration
Bermuda Business Application Forms including beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query regarding solvency or ownership, file a written reply within 14 days with updated financial evidence. If the proposed company name is unavailable, submit an alternative name reservation with the same application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form CO/1 online on the Companies House Gibraltar portal, paying the official state fee of USD 200 by corporate card. Attach the certified Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, Bermuda Certificate of No Objection, proposed Gibraltar Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the board resolution approving continuance. The form must be signed by a Bermuda director and countersigned by the Gibraltar authorised local agent.
required_dossiers: Bermuda Certificate of No Objection
Certificate of Good Standing
Proposed Gibraltar Memorandum and Articles of Association
Financial solvency statement supporting the continuance
Notice of Proposed Registered Office in Gibraltar
Board Resolution approving the continuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar queries the solvency statement or constitutional documents, file a supplementary response within 21 days together with an enhanced board affidavit and any requested amendments to the Gibraltar constitutional documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Gibraltar Registrar will issue a Certificate of Continuance, recording the company as a continuation of the Bermuda Exempted Company with a new Gibraltar company number. The certificate is conclusive evidence of continuance. Deliver a certified copy to the Bermuda Registrar within 7 days to finalise the removal of the company from the Bermuda register.
required_dossiers: Copy of the Gibraltar Certificate of Continuance
Payment receipt for the official filing fee
Confirmation order from Companies House Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any typographical or registration number error appears on the Certificate of Continuance, file Form COR/1 requesting administrative correction within 14 days of issue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Registered Office and Organise Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Licensed Registered Office Provider and Companies House Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form RO1 to record the registered office address at a licensed Gibraltar registered office. Establish the statutory registers (members, directors, secretaries, and charges), open the company seal, prepare the first board minutes, and complete the share allotment as resolved in the first board resolution. Publish a notice of continuance in the Gibraltar Gazette as required by law.
required_dossiers: Registered office acceptance letter or lease
Consent to Act forms for each director, CEO, CFO, and Company Secretary
Shareholders register and ledger
Form RO1 (registered office filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is rejected by the Registrar, appoint an alternative licensed services provider and refile Form RO1 within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Gibraltar Income Tax Office and Obtain Tax Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate tax registration application together with the Certificate of Continuance and the Bermuda tax exemption certificate. Request written confirmation that the company, being managed and controlled outside Gibraltar, is not considered Gibraltar tax resident. This step preserves the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification and is required for the online payment rail due diligence.
required_dossiers: Gibraltar Certificate of Continuance
Bermuda tax exemption certificate
Certified list of directors and shareholders
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Board minutes evidencing management and control outside Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commissioner contends that central management and control is in Gibraltar, provide detailed board minutes, physical presence evidence, and travel records to demonstrate management in Bermuda. Apply for a formal determination within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank or EMI Account and Onboard Payment Processors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (AML registration); licensed Gibraltar banks and authorised EMI institutions; Stripe and PayPal merchant onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a corporate banking application with a Gibraltar-licensed bank or EMI supporting GBP/EUR settlement, submitting the Certificate of Continuance, constitutional documents, beneficial ownership declaration, and the board resolution approving signatories. File an AML registration with the GFSC if the entity falls within the designated non-financial business sector. Thereafter, configure Stripe and PayPal merchant accounts under the company's registered name using supporting corporate documents.
required_dossiers: Gibraltar Certificate of Continuance
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certificate of Tax Status
Board resolution approving bank accounts and merchant payment processors
Passport and proof of residence for each director and officer
AML/CFT compliance policy and risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor flags the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier for jewellery trading, submit an enhanced due diligence file containing supply-chain invoices, storefront URLs, customer refund policy, and historical ownership records to satisfy the enhanced KYC request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no physical manufacturing or industrial facility is operated; the business activity is exclusively online merchandising under ISIC 4791.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – no operating or manufacturing permit is mandated for e-commerce retail of jewellery and timepieces.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Gibraltar Environmental Agency, Department of the Environment, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA Exempt – Category 3 (Online retail and warehousing); registration only is required for packaging waste compliance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or industrial discharges. Packaging waste must be recovered in accordance with the Packaging Waste (Gibraltar) Regulations; any incidental volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from warehousing remain below the registration threshold of 100 kg per year.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the Gibraltar registered office and any storage area, the following clearances apply: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire and Rescue Services Ordinance, electrical load and safety inspection certificate, and a general workplace health and safety risk assessment. No civil defense or structural load clearance applies because no heavy industrial processing is undertaken.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax) — official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation; HM Customs Gibraltar — official portal: https://www.customs.gi; parent-state reference for goods entering the United Kingdom customs territory: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/hm-revenue-customs
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Bermuda Exempted Company as an oversea company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under Part XXIII of the Companies Act 2014 to obtain a Gibraltar company number. Step 2: Engage a Gibraltar-resident tax agent and file with the Income Tax Office the certified certificate of incorporation issued by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies, the annotated memorandum and articles of association, the register of directors, and a board resolution appointing a Gibraltar-resident company manager. Step 3: Obtain the Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN) and, where physical goods movement is anticipated, an Economic Operator Registration and Identification (EORI) reference from HM Customs Gibraltar. Step 4: File the annual Bermuda exempted-company return (EB form) and pay the Bermuda annual government fee to preserve the entity's tax-exempt status; no minimum share capital or paid-up capital requirement applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' election. Available mechanisms: (a) Bermuda — election for the Exempted Company to be designated as a 'permit company' under the Bermuda Companies Act 1981, allowing limited domestic business activity without losing exempt status; (b) Gibraltar — election or factual filing to maintain non-resident status where central management and control is exercised outside Gibraltar, and the 'qualifying company' procedure for any Gibraltar-incorporated subsidiary; (c) hybrid mismatch — no elective domestic check-the-box election; Gibraltar applies the OECD hybrid and branch mismatch rules automatically under its domestic anti-hybrid legislation, while the UK parent regime (Corporation Tax Act 2010, s. 259) allows a hybridity notice only in a narrow foreign-branch mismatch case.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar Customs and Excise Duty Regime (non-VAT jurisdiction; no general VAT, GST, or sales and use tax is levied within Gibraltar; indirect taxation is limited to import duties and excise duties on specified goods).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — Gibraltar imposes no VAT/GST and therefore no turnover-based indirect tax registration threshold; any business importing or exporting commercial goods must obtain an EORI number from HM Customs Gibraltar at a nil registration threshold, and operators handling excise goods (alcohol, tobacco, fuel) require a licence under the Excise Duty Ordinance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate is in force in Gibraltar. Customs declarations are submitted electronically in a machine-readable format approved by HM Customs Gibraltar through the Gibraltar electronic customs declaration gateway; e-commerce invoices and payment records for the fashion jewelry and watch business must be retained for six years under the Income Tax Act, but no government real-time API clearance or e-invoicing platform applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Strictly, there is no VAT zero-rating in Gibraltar. Export relief applies to goods physically leaving Gibraltar, placing the supply outside the scope of Gibraltar customs and excise duties. For jewelry, watches, and fashion items sold online and shipped to non-resident consumers, the exporter must evidence physical departure from Gibraltar, lodgement of a valid export declaration, and settlement of proceeds in a freely convertible currency. Where import duty was paid at the time of importation into Gibraltar, a drawback or remission is available only upon production of export evidence within the statutory time limits. UK import VAT may arise separately at the consignment's arrival in Great Britain and is administered by HMRC, independent of the Gibraltar regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar export declaration (C88 equivalent) lodged through the electronic customs declaration gateway of HM Customs Gibraltar
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (original or signed shipped-on-board copy)
Commercial invoice and itemised packing list issued by the Bermuda Exempted Company
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank credit advice, or Stripe/PayPal settlement report evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the designated Gibraltar or Bermuda bank account
Bermuda Economic Substance (ES) annual declaration and annual exempted-company government fee receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating or export-relief claims are prosecuted under Gibraltar's customs and excise legislation: civil penalties of up to GBP 25,000 or three times the duty evaded, seizure and forfeiture of goods, vehicles, and associated digital or electronic-money assets; criminal liability carries up to seven years' imprisonment and an unlimited fine; any drawback or duty remission granted is retrospectively clawed back with a 100% surcharge. A Bermuda Exempted Company making false export declarations further risks penalties of USD 10,000 to USD 250,000 per annum under the Bermuda Economic Substance Act 2018, potential strike-off, and retrospective reclassification as Gibraltar-resident where central management and control is shown to be exercised in Gibraltar, exposing deemed profits to 12.5% Gibraltar corporation tax plus interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar / HM Treasury (monetary authority) and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the integrated financial services regulator for banking, investment, and e-money activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange control laws, mandatory approvals, or central bank transfer restrictions. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, intercompany loan repayments, and capital repatriation may be executed freely through the banking system, subject to standard anti-money laundering documentation such as board resolutions, source of funds evidence, and CRS/FATCA declarations. The Gibraltar pound is pegged at par to pound sterling and GBP/EUR/USD conversion occurs at commercial bank rates. As a Bermuda Exempted Company, no Gibraltar corporate income tax is levied, but any claim of non-Gibraltar tax residence must be supported by central management and control documentation and, if applicable, economic substance evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists in Gibraltar. Export receipts may be retained in original currency or converted at the exporter's discretion. There are no mandatory conversion ratios or repatriation timelines. Only general AML/CTF reporting thresholds, sanctions screening, and record-keeping obligations apply to trade-related inward payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Precious Metals Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for regulated Gibraltar-licensed and UK-authorized e-money institutions, which can support marketplace payouts, virtual IBANs, and SEPA/Faster Payments. Low viability for unregulated offshore digital EMIs because they cannot lawfully hold client funds, issue payment instruments, or provide merchant settlement rails in Gibraltar without an FSC licence. Third-country EMI passporting into Gibraltar is restricted after Brexit, so a Gibraltar e-money licence or UK EMI authorisation is the legally preferred route.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar banks require physical presence or a formal video interview under enhanced due diligence. For a Bermuda Exempted Company engaged in medium-risk e-commerce, at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner must normally appear in person before a bank officer or an accredited external introducer. Remote account opening is accepted only for existing private-banking clients, provided original certified corporate documents, notarised KYC forms, and source-of-wealth evidence are filed before activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value goods and fashion e-commerce classification triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Itemised product catalogue with HS/ISIC mapping, third-party valuation certificates for fine timepieces and jewellery, supplier invoices, delivery and insurance documentation, and audited transaction histories to demonstrate lawful trade and consistent revenue streams.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the Bermuda Exempted Company shareholding and ultimate beneficial ownership layer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, register of directors and shareholders, trust deed if applicable, UBO declaration form, source of wealth statement, and the first capital injection wire together with the underlying board resolution and share allotment records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to payment aggregators, cross-border marketplaces, and potential sanctions circumvention
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed payment processor agreements, end-to-end transaction flow diagrams, sanctions screening policy, OFAC/UK/HMG sanctions lists check, geolocation and IP verification data, and a written enterprise AML policy approved by the board.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the ultimate beneficial owner or parent entity in EUR, GBP, or USD. The wire reference must identify 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - [ENTITY NAME]' and be supported by a current board resolution, share allotment letter, and, where relevant, an intercompany loan agreement. For payments from EU jurisdictions, SEPA Credit Transfer may be used for amounts below EUR 100,000, but the remitter must include the purpose code for direct investment or capital contribution. All within bank-to-bank sanctions screening and FATCA/CRS self-certification requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to suppliers and third-party vendors should use SWIFT MT103 with corresponding purpose code for goods and services. For jewellery and timepiece procurement, suppliers in Asia or high-risk jurisdictions may require an irrevocable, confirmed commercial letter of credit at sight, with payment via MT103/MT202 under the LC terms. Disbursements to e-commerce logistics providers and marketplaces may be executed through commercial payment processors, PayPal or Stripe, with funds swept daily into the Gibraltar operational account. Currency conversions must be explicitly agreed at the time of the trade to avoid unfavourable spot rates, and all outbound payments must match the supporting invoices and import/export documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts (against GBP, EUR, USD, and liquid trade counterpart currencies)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market supplier currencies with transferability controls
Cross-currency swaps (principal and interest) for longer-dated working capital and intercompany loan obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Annual Return (Form AR) and annual exempted-company government fee (BMD 2,640) accompanied by the BMD 100 filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Financial Services Department, Government of Bermuda, submitted electronically via the licensed Bermuda registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within six months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year company with a 31 December year-end the deadline is 30 June of the following year; the annual government fee covers the 1 January to 31 December fee period and is payable with the return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative late fees apply under the Registrar's fee schedule, with continuing daily default charges; persistent default after reminder notice triggers strike-off under Section 203 of the Companies Act 1981, loss of the Certificate of Compliance, and termination of the Bermuda registered office and resident agent relationship.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance (Requirements) Act annual filing and registration confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Economic Substance Authority, administered through the Registrar of Companies on the portal managed by the Bermuda International Business Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year, aligned with the Annual Return deadline (30 June for a 31 December financial year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Strict-liability penalty of BMD 17,700 for failure to file or for incomplete or inaccurate filing, with a further BMD 17,700 sanction for each additional year of non-compliance; sustained violation results in an official non-compliance declaration, public disclosure, and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Declaration and 14-day update mechanism following shareholding transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda, filed through an approved Beneficial Ownership Registrant on the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration due within 14 days of incorporation; annual confirmation due together with the Annual Return within six months after financial year-end; any shareholding transfer or change to registered beneficial-ownership details must be reported within 14 calendar days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register, confirm, or update beneficial ownership attracts a fine of up to BMD 1,777 per offence plus a continuing default penalty of BMD 71 per day; deliberate concealment of a reportable transfer may lead to strike-off and regulatory referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return of a Foreign Company, including schedule of members and directors, applicable while the Bermuda exempted company maintains a registered establishment in Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Civil and Commercial Registry (Companies House Gibraltar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 42 days after the anniversary of the initial registration of the Gibraltar establishment, with an annual confirmation required on each successive registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties escalate under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 schedule from approximately GBP 30 to GBP 375 depending on the period of lateness; continued default may cause the Registrar to strike off the Gibraltar establishment registration and notify the parent Bermuda registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar company income tax return, Form CT4, mandatory only if the Bermuda exempted company is tax-resident in Gibraltar through management and control or carries on trade through a Gibraltar permanent establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the accounting period, subject to the Commissioner's published effective date, commonly 30 April following a 31 December year-end; final tax is payable on the effective date or within 30 days of a notice of assessment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Best-of-judgment default assessments, late-payment surcharge of up to 50% of unpaid tax, statutory interest on overdue amounts, and criminal fines on conviction for fraudulent non-disclosure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The Bermuda Companies Act 1981 does not impose a statutory audit on a non-regulated, non-listed exempted company; audit becomes compulsory for licensed banks, insurance undertakings, digital asset businesses, fund administrators, and BSX-listed issuers. In Gibraltar, an audit becomes mandatory if the company meets the Gibraltar Companies Act medium/large company thresholds, namely annual turnover above GBP 8.7 million, balance sheet total over GBP 4.4 million, or 50 or more employees. For this medium-risk e-commerce profile, no statutory audit is expected, but the acquiring bank or electronic money institution may contractually require a certified audit once gross annual throughput exceeds USD 1 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, with US GAAP also accepted in Bermuda for non-regulated exempted companies; if the company becomes Gibraltar tax-resident or files Gibraltar accounts, the applicable framework is IFRS as recognized in Gibraltar or FRS 102/UK GAAP for a small company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2024, the exempted company must file a Beneficial Ownership Declaration through a licensed Registrant within 14 days of incorporation, reconfirm the declaration annually with the Annual Return, and file an update within 14 calendar days of any transfer of shares or change of ownership details. A Gibraltar establishment, if maintained, must keep a register of persons with significant control and file an annual confirmation with the Gibraltar Registrar, mirroring the UK PSC regime.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Bermuda registered office and resident agent: USD 1,800 to USD 2,500 per annum; Gibraltar licensed registered establishment (if maintained): USD 1,500 to USD 3,000 per annum
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 per annum for a non-listed, non-regulated Bermuda exempted company; an additional GBP 4,000 to GBP 10,000 equivalent applies if a Gibraltar entity audit or consolidated accounts are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar levies a flat 10% corporate income tax. A Qualifying Company election permits a 0% rate on income arising outside Gibraltar, provided the company has no Gibraltar-source income and meets the qualifying conditions; an annual GB£925 fee applies. Additionally, no capital gains tax, gift tax, or inheritance tax is imposed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Company Tax Return (Form C1) submitted via the iTax electronic filing portal of the Income Tax Office (Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within seven months after the end of the company's accounting period; e.g., a 31 December year-end is due by 31 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification details: legal name, registered number, registered office, tax reference number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Gibraltar branch or representative details; if no permanent establishment, insert 'Non-resident – no Gibraltar PE' and request a Certificate of Residence if treaty relief is sought.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates (YYYY-MM-DD).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the actual accounting period of the Bermuda exempted company; align with the financial statements used for the filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross trading receipts/sales from online supply of jewelry, watches and fashion accessories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only profits attributable to a permanent establishment in Gibraltar. If the company is a Qualifying Company asserting foreign-source income, mark the QC status and report Gibraltar-source turnover separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-adjusted profit/loss (income after deductions, capital allowances, and loss relief).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute in accordance with Gibraltar law; for a QC, taxable profits on foreign sources are excluded, so enter '0' on the taxable line but provide full reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 10% (or at 0% if valid QC election).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident companies without a PE, enter nil; if PE profits exist, apply the 10% rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by director/company secretary and date; includes signature and capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The signed declaration attests that the return is complete and accurate; a director of the Bermuda exempted company must sign, even if located overseas.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic fixed penalty of GB£100, escalating to GB£300 after three months and further daily penalties up to a maximum of GB£500; late-paid tax attracts interest at 8% per annum from the due date until payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Gibraltar does not impose a domestic withholding tax on dividends paid by Gibraltar companies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced foreign withholding tax on overseas dividends/interest/royalties, the Gibraltar-resident beneficial owner applies to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a Certificate of Residence (TRC), usually via the iTax portal, evidencing tax residence and economic substance; the certificate is then submitted with the foreign tax authority's relief form before or within the foreign statutory deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law: 0% withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest. Under double tax agreements, the typical limit ranges from 0% to 10%; for example, the UK-Gibraltar DTA generally caps interest and royalty withholding at 0% for beneficial owners resident in the other state, subject to TRC and no-PE conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Gibraltar has no statutory transfer pricing documentation threshold for Local File/Master File; however, OECD-aligned documentation is recommended for controlled transactions exceeding GB£1,000,000. MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million are subject to Country-by-Country Reporting obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (Requirements) Regulations 2018 apply to Gibraltar tax-resident companies engaged in relevant activities, including distribution and services; an online jewelry e-commerce business is a 'relevant activity' requiring physical presence in Gibraltar (employees, premises, expenditure) proportionate to the level of such activity. Qualifying Companies claiming a 0% foreign-source rate must demonstrate that no economic substance is present in Gibraltar and that core income-generating activities take place in the jurisdiction of their actual management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally failing to record or understating turnover from Stripe/PayPal settlement of jewelry and timepiece sales, thereby reducing Gibraltar taxable income below the real figure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under Gibraltar's Income Tax Act as extended by the Criminal Justice Act; liability to pay underdeclared tax, a tax-geared penalty of up to double the amount of tax evaded, and/or a fine of up to GB£100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly procure fraudulent returns face unlimited joint and several liability for the company's unpaid tax plus civil recovery; travel restrictions and a custodial sentence of up to 7 years may be imposed. The corporate veil is pierced for sham/fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Gibraltar-resident e-commerce entity structured as a Bermuda Exempted Company that maintains only a mailbox, has no employees or premises in Gibraltar, but uses the Gibraltar QC regime to claim 0% tax on foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The QC election is invalid; all foreign-source profits become taxable at 10%; in addition, the Income Tax Office may impose a penalty of GB£10,000 for failure to comply with the Economic Substance Regulations and issue a notice requiring remedial action within 60 days.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for penalties if the substance requirements are knowingly omitted; they can be disqualified as directors in Gibraltar for up to 15 years and be named in public notices; serious non-compliance attracts criminal sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The online jewelry/timepiece business fails to implement customer due diligence, record-keeping, and suspicious transaction reporting required for 'high-value dealers' under Gibraltar's Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and AML/CFT Regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil monetary penalties of up to GB£5 million or 10% of global turnover; criminal conviction can result in a fine and/or imprisonment up to 2 years; license termination and closure of the e-commerce payment processors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are subject to individual civil penalties; where non-compliance is a deliberate act of money laundering facilitation, directors face prosecution with imprisonment up to 14 years, forfeiture of personal assets, and regulatory debarment from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing of IP Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Gibraltar company pays excessive management, trademark or IP royalties to an affiliated holding company in a zero-tax jurisdiction to strip taxable profit from the Gibraltar e-commerce business, deviating from arm's length third-party prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the controlled transaction; taxable profits increased; a transfer pricing penalty of 100% of the additional tax due on the adjustment plus interest at 8% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's length arrangements can be made personally liable for the increased tax and penalties if the company becomes insolvent; also possible criminal liability for tax evasion by intentionally mispricing.
